newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian Labor opposes a quarter of budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian Labor opposes a quarter of budget cuts.

text.p: Australia's Labor Opposition said on Friday it had decided to vote against measures worth about a quarter of the government's planned fiscal tightening.
"The government's total fiscal consolidation programme as it's been identified is on our estimate A$23.4 billion," opposition treasury spokesman Gareth Evans told reporters.
"We estimate the total impact of all the measures we are proposing to oppose -- if we were successful in opposing them, obviously -- as being A$7.3 billion over that period," he said.
Evans's estimate referred to the value of fiscal measures over the four years from June 1996.
The government announced spending cuts and revenue hike in the August 20 budget with the aim of producing a A$1 billion fiscal surplus in the year to June 1999.
The Liberal-National government is two seats short of a majority in the Senate, the upper house of parliament, whose consent will be needed for any legislative changes to support the budget.
The extra two votes can come from Labor, the small Australian Democrats party, two loosely united Greens or a pair of Independents.
The Senate's acquiesence to spending cuts can be taken for granted, since it can block them only by opposing supply bills, an action that would spark a constitutional crisis.
